tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting up a jar test to compare coagulant doses on today's raw water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional Ontario surface water plant. Raw water is collected at the intake sample tap for a bench jar test.
tasks.configuration: Fictional Ontario surface water plant. Raw water is collected at the intake sample tap for a bench jar test.

cards.label: Collect a representative raw water sample and record its temperature, pH, turbidity and alkalinity
Fill each jar with the same measured volume of raw water
Add a different measured coagulant dose to each jar
Rapid mix all jars at the same speed and time to disperse the coagulant
Slow mix all jars to allow floc to form
Stop mixing and allow the jars to settle for the set settling time
Measure settled water turbidity in each jar and record the results

tasks.explanation: A representative sample and equal jar volumes make the doses comparable. Rapid mix disperses coagulant, slow mix builds floc, settling follows, and turbidity is measured only after settling.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for selecting a plant coagulant dose from completed jar test results.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Six jars were dosed in increasing amounts and settled turbidity results are available.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Six jars were dosed in increasing amounts and settled turbidity results are available.

cards.label: Review the settled turbidity and floc appearance recorded for each jar dose
Identify the lowest dose that produced clear settled water and strong floc
Check that the selected dose leaves adequate residual alkalinity in the treated sample
Confirm the selected dose against current raw water conditions before changing the plant feed
Adjust the plant coagulant feeder to the selected dose
Monitor settled water turbidity after the change and record the new dose in the log

tasks.explanation: Dose selection starts from the jar results, checks alkalinity, confirms raw water has not changed, and only then changes the plant feed, with monitoring and logging last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a jar test run when raw water alkalinity is low.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Raw alkalinity is near the lower end of the normal range before a coagulant trial.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Raw alkalinity is near the lower end of the normal range before a coagulant trial.

cards.label: Measure raw water alkalinity and pH before dosing any jars
Calculate the alkalinity expected to be consumed by the trial coagulant doses
Add alkali to the jars that need it to hold the target coagulation pH
Add the coagulant doses and run the rapid mix and slow mix sequence
Measure settled pH and turbidity in each jar after settling
Select the dose and alkali combination that met both pH and turbidity targets

tasks.explanation: Alkalinity and its consumption must be known before dosing, because coagulation pH controls performance. Settled pH and turbidity are judged together at the end.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for building a seasonal jar test baseline before spring runoff.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant preparing for spring runoff. Historical raw water records and bench equipment are available.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant preparing for spring runoff. Historical raw water records and bench equipment are available.

cards.label: Review last year's runoff records for turbidity, colour and alkalinity ranges
Select trial dose ranges that cover the expected runoff conditions
Run jar tests across the selected dose ranges on current raw water
Record the dose response results in the seasonal baseline table
Set the starting plant dose and feeder settings from the baseline before runoff arrives

tasks.explanation: Planning uses history first, then bench trials, then a recorded baseline, and plant settings are set from that baseline before the event arrives.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a full scale coagulant dose optimization trial over one shift.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant running a planned dose trial at steady flow with the supervisor's approval.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant running a planned dose trial at steady flow with the supervisor's approval.

cards.label: Record baseline settled and filtered turbidity at the current dose
Change the coagulant dose by one planned step only
Wait for the changed water to travel through the flocculation and sedimentation basins
Record settled and filtered turbidity at the new dose
Compare the new results with the baseline and decide whether to keep or revert the dose
Log the trial steps, results and decision in the plant record

tasks.explanation: A baseline must exist before a change, travel time must pass before sampling, and comparison and logging complete the trial.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for jar testing a flocculant aid with the plant coagulant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. A polymer aid is being bench tested as a supplement to the normal coagulant.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. A polymer aid is being bench tested as a supplement to the normal coagulant.

cards.label: Prepare the polymer solution to the supplier's stated concentration and record it
Dose all jars with the same coagulant amount
Rapid mix the jars to disperse the coagulant
Add a different measured polymer dose to each jar at the start of slow mixing
Slow mix, settle, and measure settled turbidity in each jar
Select the polymer dose with the best floc and settled clarity without overdosing

tasks.explanation: Polymer is added after coagulant dispersion and at the start of flocculation, matching plant practice. Selection follows settling and measurement.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running duplicate jar tests as a quality check.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant laboratory. Two operators will run the same jar test series for comparison.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant laboratory. Two operators will run the same jar test series for comparison.

cards.label: Agree on one written procedure, dose series and mixing times for both runs
Collect one large raw water sample and split it evenly between the two runs
Run the first jar series and record all results
Run the second jar series using the same procedure on the split sample
Compare the duplicate results jar by jar
Investigate any large differences and record the agreed result

tasks.explanation: A shared procedure and a split sample remove avoidable differences before the runs. Comparison comes after both runs, and investigation follows comparison.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a jar test that compares coagulation at different pH values.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Raw water colour is high and coagulation pH is being studied on the bench.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Raw water colour is high and coagulation pH is being studied on the bench.

cards.label: Fill the jars with equal volumes of the same raw water sample
Adjust each jar to a different target pH and record the amount used
Add the same coagulant dose to every jar
Rapid mix, slow mix and settle all jars under identical conditions
Measure settled turbidity and colour in each jar
Identify the pH that gave the best settled quality for plant follow up

tasks.explanation: Only pH varies between jars, so pH is adjusted before the common dose and identical mixing. The best pH is identified from the settled results.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for putting a new jar test dose into service on the plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. A jar test has identified a better coagulant dose and the change is approved.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. A jar test has identified a better coagulant dose and the change is approved.

cards.label: Confirm the jar test result with a repeat check of current raw water turbidity and alkalinity
Calculate the feeder setting needed to deliver the new dose at current plant flow
Adjust the feeder and verify the actual feed rate by a drawdown or calibration check
Watch floc formation and settled turbidity through one basin travel time
Record the old dose, new dose, reason and time of change in the operating log

tasks.explanation: The bench result is confirmed against current raw water first, the feeder setting is calculated and verified, performance is watched, and the change is logged last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a supervisor review of a week of jar test records.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. The supervisor is reviewing bench records against plant performance for the past week.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. The supervisor is reviewing bench records against plant performance for the past week.

cards.label: Collect the week's jar test sheets and the matching plant dose logs
Match each jar test result to the plant dose that was in use at that time
Compare settled turbidity predicted by the jars with actual plant settled turbidity
Flag any days where plant results differed greatly from jar predictions
Record follow up actions for the flagged days and file the review

tasks.explanation: Records are collected and matched before comparison, differences are flagged from the comparison, and follow up is recorded last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a first response to flooding in the plant basement gallery.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Water is entering a below grade gallery during a storm.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Water is entering a below grade gallery during a storm.

cards.label: Keep staff clear of electrical hazards and stop work in the flooded area
Isolate electrical equipment in the affected area if it can be done safely
Start sump or portable pumps to control the water level
Notify the supervisor and record the extent and equipment affected
Inspect and test affected equipment before returning it to service after the water is cleared

tasks.explanation: Personnel safety and electrical isolation come first, pumping controls the water, the event is escalated and recorded, and equipment is proven safe before reuse.

tasks.prompt: Order the response steps when raw water turbidity rises sharply during a storm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional surface water plant. Raw turbidity has doubled in one hour and rain continues.
tasks.configuration: Fictional surface water plant. Raw turbidity has doubled in one hour and rain continues.

cards.label: Confirm the rise with a grab sample and a second turbidity measurement
Notify the supervisor and note the time and readings in the log
Run a quick jar test on the new raw water to check the coagulant dose
Adjust the coagulant feed to the dose supported by the jar test
Increase monitoring of settled and filtered turbidity
Review the dose again once raw turbidity stabilizes

tasks.explanation: Verification comes before escalation and dose changes. The dose is set from a fresh jar test, monitoring increases, and review follows stabilization.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for responding to a sudden rise in raw water colour from runoff.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. True colour has risen well above normal after heavy rain in the watershed.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. True colour has risen well above normal after heavy rain in the watershed.

cards.label: Measure raw colour, turbidity, pH and alkalinity on a fresh sample
Jar test a range of coagulant doses for colour removal
Select the dose that met colour and turbidity targets in the jars
Adjust the plant coagulant feed and confirm the feeder output
Monitor settled colour and turbidity until they return to target

tasks.explanation: Fresh measurements define the event, jar tests set the dose, the feed is adjusted and verified, and monitoring continues to target.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for adjusting coagulation as raw water temperature falls in late autumn.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Raw water temperature has fallen below 5 degrees C and floc is forming slowly.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Raw water temperature has fallen below 5 degrees C and floc is forming slowly.

cards.label: Confirm the temperature trend from intake records over several days
Jar test current raw water at its actual cold temperature
Review floc formation time and settled quality in the cold jars
Adjust dose or aid and flocculation time based on the cold water results
Monitor plant floc and settled turbidity more frequently through the change

tasks.explanation: Cold water slows reactions, so the trend is confirmed and jars are run at actual temperature before plant changes are made and monitored.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps when raw water alkalinity drops during spring melt.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Snowmelt has diluted raw alkalinity and coagulation pH is falling.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Snowmelt has diluted raw alkalinity and coagulation pH is falling.

cards.label: Measure raw alkalinity and treated pH and compare with normal ranges
Calculate the alkali feed needed to hold the target coagulation pH
Start or increase the alkali feed and verify its output
Recheck coagulation pH and settled turbidity after one travel time
Log the alkalinity trend, feed change and results

tasks.explanation: Measurement and calculation precede the feed change, verification follows one travel time later, and logging completes the response.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for responding to an algae bloom affecting coagulation.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional reservoir source plant. Algae counts are high and filters are seeing extra load.
tasks.configuration: Fictional reservoir source plant. Algae counts are high and filters are seeing extra load.

cards.label: Confirm the bloom with raw water algae observations and taste and odour checks
Jar test to check coagulant demand and floc settleability with the algae present
Adjust coagulant or aid dose based on the jar results
Watch clarifier sludge blanket and settled turbidity for algae carryover
Shorten filter runs as needed based on headloss and effluent turbidity trends

tasks.explanation: The bloom is confirmed first, demand is bench tested, plant dose follows, and clarifier and filter effects are managed from observed trends.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps when the rapid mix unit fails during operation.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. The rapid mixer motor has tripped and coagulant is still feeding.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. The rapid mixer motor has tripped and coagulant is still feeding.

cards.label: Stop the coagulant feed to the unmixed application point
Notify the supervisor and log the time of the failure
Switch coagulant feed to the approved alternate mixing point if one is available
Restart or repair the mixer following the maintenance procedure
Confirm mixing is restored and floc is forming normally before returning to the normal feed point

tasks.explanation: Feeding into an unmixed point wastes chemical and harms treatment, so feed stops first. Normal feed resumes only after mixing is confirmed restored.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for adjusting flocculation energy when floc is breaking up.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Large floc forms early in the basin but arrives at the outlet as small pin floc.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Large floc forms early in the basin but arrives at the outlet as small pin floc.

cards.label: Observe floc size at the basin inlet, middle and outlet
Check current paddle or mixer speeds against the operating guide
Reduce the speed in the later flocculation zone by one step
Observe floc at the outlet after allowing the adjusted water to travel through
Record the speed change and the floc response in the log

tasks.explanation: Observation along the basin locates the breakup, speeds are checked, one change is made, its effect is observed after travel time, and the change is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for investigating rising settled water turbidity at steady flow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Settled turbidity has risen over two hours with no flow change.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Settled turbidity has risen over two hours with no flow change.

cards.label: Verify the settled turbidity reading with a grab sample on a bench meter
Check coagulant feed rate and day tank level for an interruption
Check raw turbidity, alkalinity and coagulation pH for a source change
Inspect floc formation and the clarifier sludge blanket depth
Correct the cause found and monitor settled turbidity back to target

tasks.explanation: The reading is verified first, then chemical feed, source water and basin condition are checked in flow order, and correction and monitoring follow.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing coagulation and clarification for a planned high flow period.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Demand will rise to near rated capacity for the next day.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Demand will rise to near rated capacity for the next day.

cards.label: Confirm the expected flow and duration with the distribution operator
Check chemical inventories and feeder capacity for the higher dose rates
Jar test at the expected conditions to confirm dose at high flow
Raise clarifier sludge wasting to keep the blanket low before the event
Monitor settled turbidity and blanket depth closely during the high flow period

tasks.explanation: The event is defined first, chemical capacity is confirmed, dose is bench checked, the clarifier is prepared, and close monitoring covers the event itself.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps when the duty coagulant feed pump fails.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. The duty coagulant pump has stopped and the standby pump is available.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. The duty coagulant pump has stopped and the standby pump is available.

cards.label: Confirm the failure by checking pump status, feed line flow and day tank drawdown
Start the standby coagulant pump and set it to the required feed rate
Verify chemical is reaching the application point and floc is forming
Notify the supervisor and maintenance and log the failure and changeover
Tag out the failed pump for repair following lockout procedures

tasks.explanation: Changeover to the standby pump restores treatment first and is verified at the application point. Notification, logging and tag out follow.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for extending filter runs without losing effluent quality.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant with four rapid gravity filters and individual effluent turbidimeters.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant with four rapid gravity filters and individual effluent turbidimeters.

cards.label: Review run length, headloss and effluent turbidity records for each filter
Identify the filter that ends runs with quality and headloss margin remaining
Extend that filter's run target by a small planned amount
Monitor its effluent turbidity and headloss closely through the longer run
Adopt, adjust or abandon the new target based on the recorded results

tasks.explanation: Records identify the candidate, a small trial extension follows, close monitoring covers the trial, and the decision is based on results.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking a filter out of service for backwash.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. One filter has reached its headloss limit and is due for backwash.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. One filter has reached its headloss limit and is due for backwash.

cards.label: Confirm the backwash trigger from headloss, turbidity or run time records
Check that the remaining filters can carry the plant flow during the wash
Notify the control room and log the filter coming out of service
Close the filter influent and allow the water level to draw down to the wash level
Begin the backwash sequence for that filter

tasks.explanation: The trigger is confirmed, capacity of the remaining filters is checked, the change is communicated and logged, the filter is drawn down, and washing begins.

tasks.prompt: Order the stages of a standard air and water backwash for a dual media filter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional dual media filter with air scour and surface wash fitted, following the plant wash procedure.
tasks.configuration: Fictional dual media filter with air scour and surface wash fitted, following the plant wash procedure.

cards.label: Drain the filter water down to just above the media surface
Start air scour to loosen the media bed
Start the low rate backwash water flow with air continuing
Stop the air and raise the wash water to the full backwash rate
Continue washing until the waste water runs acceptably clear
Stop the wash and allow the bed to settle and regrade

tasks.explanation: Draining precedes air scour, air and low water combine, air stops before full rate washing, washing continues to clarity, and the bed settles last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for returning a backwashed filter to service using filter to waste.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. A filter has completed backwash and has a filter to waste capability.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. A filter has completed backwash and has a filter to waste capability.

cards.label: Complete the backwash and allow the media bed to settle
Start the filter at a reduced rate with effluent directed to waste
Monitor the waste stream turbidity as the filter ripens
Confirm effluent turbidity is below the plant target for the set time
Open the filter to the clear well and raise it to its normal rate
Log the wash, ripening time and return to service

tasks.explanation: The bed settles first, ripening runs to waste, quality must meet target before the clear well is opened, rate is then normalized, and the cycle is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for managing backwash waste water returned to the head of the plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant with a backwash recovery tank that returns wash water at a controlled rate.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant with a backwash recovery tank that returns wash water at a controlled rate.

cards.label: Confirm the recovery tank level and that the return pumps are available
Check the recovered water turbidity before starting the return
Start the return at the set percentage of plant inflow
Monitor raw water turbidity and coagulant demand while the return is running
Stop or reduce the return if settled turbidity rises above target

tasks.explanation: Tank and pump readiness and water quality are checked before return starts. The return rate is controlled and its effect on treatment is monitored with a stop rule.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a step test to check a filter's response to a higher rate.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant evaluating a modest filtration rate increase on one filter.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant evaluating a modest filtration rate increase on one filter.

cards.label: Record baseline effluent turbidity and headloss at the current rate
Increase the filter rate by one planned step
Hold the new rate for the set test period
Record effluent turbidity and headloss through the test period
Return the filter to its normal rate and evaluate the results before any permanent change

tasks.explanation: Baseline data comes first, one rate step is tested and held, results are recorded, and the filter returns to normal while results are evaluated.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for an internal inspection of a drained filter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. A filter is out of service and drained for a scheduled media inspection.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. A filter is out of service and drained for a scheduled media inspection.

cards.label: Isolate, drain and lock out the filter following the plant procedure
Enter and inspect the media surface for cracks, mounding and mudballs
Measure media depth at several points and compare with the design depth
Inspect the underdrain area and nozzles where access allows
Record findings, photograph the surface and report any defects for repair planning

tasks.explanation: Safe isolation and draining precede entry. Surface, depth and underdrain checks follow in order, and findings are recorded and reported last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for checking underdrain performance during a backwash observation.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Uneven boiling is suspected during backwash on one filter.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Uneven boiling is suspected during backwash on one filter.

cards.label: Start the backwash and observe the bed surface as wash water rises
Map the areas of strong, weak and no upward flow across the surface
Stop the wash and drain the filter for a closer inspection of the suspect area
Inspect nozzles or laterals in the suspect area for blockage or damage
Record the findings and raise a work order for any defects found

tasks.explanation: The wash observation locates suspect areas first. Draining and direct inspection follow, and findings and work orders complete the check.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for adjusting the backwash program for summer algae season.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Summer runs are shorter and wash water use is being reviewed before the season.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Summer runs are shorter and wash water use is being reviewed before the season.

cards.label: Review last summer's run lengths, wash frequency and wash water volumes
Set seasonal backwash triggers for headloss, turbidity and maximum run time
Adjust wash duration steps based on waste water clarity records
Brief all shifts on the seasonal triggers and steps
Review wash water use and filter quality monthly through the season

tasks.explanation: Last season's records inform the new triggers and durations. Staff are briefed before the season, and monthly review checks the program in use.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for returning a filter to service after media maintenance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Media was topped up and a nozzle replaced on an out of service filter.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Media was topped up and a nozzle replaced on an out of service filter.

cards.label: Confirm the maintenance work is complete and all tools and materials are removed
Refill the filter slowly from below to avoid disturbing the media
Backwash the filter to clean and regrade the media
Run the filter to waste until effluent turbidity meets the target
Return the filter to service and log the maintenance and restart

tasks.explanation: Completion and clearance come first, slow refill protects the bed, washing cleans it, ripening to waste proves quality, and return to service is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps in a daily filter surveillance round.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant with individual filter turbidimeters and headloss gauges.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant with individual filter turbidimeters and headloss gauges.

cards.label: Review the overnight effluent turbidity and headloss trends for all filters
Visit each filter and compare gauge readings with the recorded trends
Check each filter's rate and water level against its set points
Note any filter with rising turbidity, rapid headloss or uneven surface
Record the round findings and flag any filter needing follow up

tasks.explanation: Trend review guides the round, field readings are compared with trends, abnormalities are noted, and findings and follow ups are recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for investigating one filter with slowly rising effluent turbidity.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Filter 3 effluent turbidity has crept up over two days while other filters are stable.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Filter 3 effluent turbidity has crept up over two days while other filters are stable.

cards.label: Verify the reading with a grab sample on a calibrated bench turbidimeter
Compare Filter 3 settled water quality and rate with the other filters
Review its last backwash record for wash duration and waste clarity
Inspect the media surface at the next drawdown for mudballs or cracks
Decide on an early backwash, extended wash or maintenance based on the findings

tasks.explanation: Verification rules out instrument error first. Comparisons, wash history and surface inspection build the case before a corrective decision is made.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for responding to a rising particle count trend on a filter effluent monitor.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant fitted with a particle counter on one filter effluent for surveillance awareness.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant fitted with a particle counter on one filter effluent for surveillance awareness.

cards.label: Confirm the trend is real by checking the counter's sample flow and recent maintenance
Compare the particle trend with the filter's effluent turbidity trend
Check for recent rate changes or hydraulic surges on that filter
Reduce the filter rate or take it out for backwash if counts keep rising
Record the trend, actions and outcome for the surveillance file

tasks.explanation: Instrument checks come first, particle and turbidity trends are compared, hydraulic causes are checked, action follows continued rise, and the event is filed.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a routine filter integrity awareness check on a granular media filter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. This is a surveillance check, not a membrane integrity test.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. This is a surveillance check, not a membrane integrity test.

cards.label: Review the filter's turbidity, headloss and run time since its last backwash
Observe a full backwash for even bed lift and boil pattern
Check the drained media surface for holes, cracks or depressions
Measure media depth and compare it with the baseline record
Record the check results and schedule any corrective work

tasks.explanation: Operating history is reviewed first, wash behaviour and surface condition are observed, depth is compared with baseline, and results and work are recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking a media core sample from a filter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. A core sample will check media condition at depth on an out of service filter.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. A core sample will check media condition at depth on an out of service filter.

cards.label: Take the filter out of service, drain it and lock it out
Mark the sampling locations on the media surface
Push the core sampler straight down through the full media depth
Withdraw the core and keep the layers in order for examination
Examine each layer for coating, mudballs and gradation change and record the findings

tasks.explanation: Safe isolation precedes sampling. Locations are marked, the core is taken through full depth, layers are kept in order, and examination and recording finish the task.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps when one filter's effluent turbidity exceeds the plant action limit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Filter 2 effluent turbidity has risen above the internal action limit of 0.3 NTU.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Filter 2 effluent turbidity has risen above the internal action limit of 0.3 NTU.

cards.label: Verify the exceedance with a grab sample on a bench turbidimeter
Remove the filter from service or reduce its rate following the plant procedure
Notify the supervisor and log the time, readings and action taken
Backwash the filter and inspect for a cause before returning it
Return it to service through filter to waste only after turbidity meets target

tasks.explanation: Verification comes first, the filter is controlled, the event is escalated and logged, cause is checked during washing, and return is through filter to waste at target quality.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for investigating headloss that builds mainly at the media surface.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. Total headloss rises quickly but clears almost fully after each backwash.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. Total headloss rises quickly but clears almost fully after each backwash.

cards.label: Review headloss growth curves from several recent runs
Check settled water turbidity and algae levels entering the filter
Observe the backwash waste for the type of material being removed
Inspect the surface layer for a mat or crust at the next drain down
Adjust pretreatment or wash steps based on the findings and record the change

tasks.explanation: Run curves and influent quality frame the problem, wash waste and surface inspection confirm it, and adjustments follow the findings.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for deciding to end a filter run early.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional plant. A filter shows rising effluent turbidity well before its headloss limit.
tasks.configuration: Fictional plant. A filter shows rising effluent turbidity well before its headloss limit.

cards.label: Confirm the turbidity rise with a repeat sample
Compare the rise with the filter's normal end of run pattern
Check that other filters can take the flow if this filter stops
End the run and take the filter to backwash
Log the early termination, the readings and the reason

tasks.explanation: The rise is confirmed and compared with normal patterns, capacity is checked, the run is ended, and the decision is logged with its reason.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps in the daily CT compliance check for a clear well.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 2 water treatment study scenario. Fictional Ontario plant using free chlorine. The daily check uses the plant CT worksheet.
tasks.configuration: Fictional Ontario plant using free chlorine. The daily check uses the plant CT worksheet.

cards.label: Record the lowest clear well chlorine residual measured for the period
Record the highest pH and the lowest temperature for the same period
Determine the contact time using clear well volume at its lowest level and the peak flow factor in the procedure
Apply the baffling factor for the clear well from the approved study
Calculate CT and compare it with the required CT from the tables for the target inactivation
Record the CT result and initial the compliance worksheet

tasks.explanation: CT uses worst case residual, pH and temperature for the same period, then contact time and baffling, then the calculation and comparison, and recording last.
